businessProblem: DHFL, a large housing finance NBFC, faces a compounding crisis of wholesale-funding liquidity stress and governance credibility damage at January 2019. The post-IL&FS NBFC sector liquidity crunch has tightened refinancing capacity, while public allegations of shell-company transactions and fund diversion have damaged market trust. The company must determine the highest-priority actions to preserve liquidity, restore governance credibility, and avoid formal regulatory intervention before the situation becomes irreversible.

evidence.finding: DHFL's wholesale funding model is acutely vulnerable to the post-IL&FS NBFC liquidity squeeze; refinancing capacity is materially constrained
Liquidity position is under pressure as lenders reassess NBFC exposure and fresh borrowing becomes increasingly difficult
Asset quality of the loan book is uncertain given publicly reported governance allegations; the true extent of any impairment is not yet determined
Ability to disburse new loans is constrained as funding access tightens; core lending operations are at risk
Market confidence in DHFL is deteriorating due to sector-wide NBFC stress compounded by company-specific governance allegations
NBFC sector broadly under pressure following IL&FS collapse; contagion risk elevating cost and availability of wholesale funding for all NBFCs

Public allegations of shell-company transactions and fund diversion have been reported (unproven at decision date); allegations represent a governance credibility risk regardless of final adjudication
No independent forensic review or governance reset has been announced in response to public allegations
Regulatory scrutiny on NBFC sector has intensified following IL&FS; governance allegations increase the risk of formal regulatory intervention against DHFL specifically

clientContext.size: Large listed housing finance company with significant retail and wholesale loan book
clientContext.revenueImpactUrgency: Critical — funding access is deteriorating rapidly; without intervention, payment obligations risk default within months

ownerConstraintProfile.bottleneckRisk: High — promoter-controlled entity with governance allegations directed at ownership and management layer
ownerConstraintProfile.followThroughRisk: High — no decisive governance action or independent review initiated despite public allegations
ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: High — governance reset requires promoters to accept external scrutiny and potential personal accountability
ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: Severely compromised — management credibility is damaged by allegations and the ability to lead a credible recovery is in question
